title: Scenario — a verification run as data, not a CLI flag (PRC-12)
description:
One `--scenario <path>` replaces the growing pile of ad-hoc main.gd flags (--paused, --select, --pick, --cursor, --scroll, --build, --speed, --chain, --ability-at, --press-at, --camera, --facings, ...). A scenario boots one anchor at one difficulty, drives a timeline of actions at chosen frames, and checks assertions against a small exported state dictionary instead of a human reading a PNG. `tools/scenario.py <path>` runs one through Godot; `--scenario` also loads directly in `scripts/main.gd`. See docs/issues/PRC-12-scenario-assertion-harness.md.

Frame vs sim time: `frame` is main.gd's own per-rendered-tick counter (what `--shot <path> <frame>` has always captured against), not sim seconds. The game runs `--fixed-fps 60`; the rules tick at DT=1/30s (sim/engine.py); the in-game speed control multiplies further (1x/2x/3x). A scenario's `frame` numbers are therefore specific to running at the default (slowest authored) speed unless a `speed` action changes it earlier in the timeline — changing speed mid-scenario changes how much sim time later frame numbers represent.

Action verb -> legacy flag mapping (each verb is a thin wrapper over the same code path the flag already used): build -> --build, select -> --select, pick -> --pick, press -> --press-at (routed through the real input pipeline, Input.parse_input_event — LF-139 — so it reaches any node's _unhandled_input, not only AnchorView's), gamepad -> no legacy flag, new for PRC-18, ability -> --ability-at, speed -> --speed, scroll -> --scroll, cursor -> --cursor, pause -> --paused, camera -> --camera, shot -> --shot, a11y -> --a11y, facings -> --facings.

`gamepad` (PRC-18) is deliberately NOT the same shape as `press`: `press` synthesizes an `InputEventAction`, which already carries the action name, so it proves `Input.parse_input_event()` reaches every node's `_unhandled_input()` (LF-139) but says nothing about whether a genuinely device-shaped event — what a real controller actually produces — is matched against `project.godot`'s `[input]` bindings the same way. `gamepad` synthesizes a real `InputEventJoypadButton` or `InputEventJoypadMotion` on device 0 (every `lf_*` gamepad binding in `project.godot` uses device 0) and routes it through the identical `Input.parse_input_event()` call. Verified standalone (a bare `--script`, no scene tree) before this was wired in: the InputMap matches a synthetic device-shaped event exactly as it matches a real one, one frame after `parse_input_event()` is called — same one-frame queueing delay as `press`/`cursor` (see those verbs' own note below) — and `Input.get_connected_joypads()` stays EMPTY throughout, i.e. no physical pad needs to be attached for this to work headlessly.

At most one `shot` action per scenario, and it must be the LAST frame anything happens on: main.gd's existing --shot machinery freezes the frame, awaits the compositor, saves the PNG and quits the process (unchanged by PRC-12) — nothing scheduled after it will ever run. An `a11y` action must share the exact same frame as the `shot` action, because the a11y analyser samples its background colours out of that PNG (CLAUDE.md).

seed.description: reserved for a future scenario that reaches the recovery draft (draft.gd's --seed); unused by the anchor timeline today, since AnchorSim carries no RNG

expr.description: dotted path into the exported state dictionary — sim.lives, sim.bus_load, sim.units_alive, sim.units.0.hp, view.camera.zoom, hud.selected, ... See AnchorView.export_state()/Hud.export_state() for the full shape. Not an expression language: no arithmetic, no arbitrary GDScript Expression — a scenario file is content (CLAUDE.md), and content that can execute is a different kind of object.

expect.description: number, string or boolean the resolved expr is compared against

tolerance.description: only meaningful for == and != on numeric expr/expect; absolute difference within this counts as equal

items.description: an lf_* input action, dispatched through Input.parse_input_event() (LF-139) so it reaches any node's _unhandled_input(), not only AnchorView's. VERIFIED: the event is queued, not delivered inline, so its effect is observable starting the FOLLOWING frame, never the frame the press itself was scheduled on -- an assertion checking what a press action did must be scheduled at press_frame + 1 or later. The cursor verb below has the same one-frame delay, for the same reason.

args.description: ["button", button_index] presses an InputEventJoypadButton on device 0 (Godot's JoyButton enum ints, e.g. 0=JOY_BUTTON_A -- the lf_build/lf_confirm binding in project.godot). ["axis", axis_index, axis_value] sends an InputEventJoypadMotion on device 0 (Godot's JoyAxis enum ints, e.g. 0=LEFT_X, 1=LEFT_Y -- the lf_up/down/left/right stick bindings; axis_value is -1.0..1.0 and defaults to 1.0 if omitted). PRC-18: unlike press above, this is a genuinely DEVICE-shaped event, not an InputEventAction -- see the schema's own top-level description for why that distinction is the point. Same one-frame queueing delay as press/cursor: an assertion checking what a gamepad action did must be scheduled at its frame + 1 or later.
